proposals.title: Seven questions around one transition
bookReference: B08-EXACT-MANUSCRIPT-SECTIONS.json: The Seven Layers at a Glance, lines 272-298
B08-EXACT-MANUSCRIPT-SECTIONS.json: The Causal Web: Why It Is a DAG, Not a Stack, lines 4460-4479
proposals.sourceSupport: The manuscript calls the layers interdependent and later describes a graph with pressures in multiple directions. V2-COPY describes the Web as a complete set of required Strands for one transition and says a whole-execution proof can cover several proof roles.
proposals.websiteMapping: Let a visitor select invoice, DEX, capped issuance, loan, or treasury, then highlight the seven layer questions around the selected financial transition. Draw explicit cross-links and group Layers 4–6 as a coupled proof-core teaching concept.
proposals.readerCopy: Explore one financial transition through seven connected questions: how its setup is formed, how its rule is expressed, what inputs it uses, how the rule is encoded, what proof is checked, which cryptographic assumptions support it, and what the consumer verifies against the transaction.
proposals.interaction: Select a case; focus each layer to reveal its question and a case-specific example. Selecting a different layer preserves the case and makes the cross-links visible.
proposals.diagram: One central transition card linked to seven labeled nodes, with visible cross-links among Layers 2–6 and a highlighted 4–6 group. Avoid vertical numbered floors or arrows that imply a fixed runtime sequence.
questions: Which layer relationships should the page draw after Opus's security fact-check?
Does the manuscript's specific fourteen-edge DAG have a sufficiently reviewed mapping for a product illustration?
proposals.limits: Educational mapping only. It does not establish seven implementation modules, a formal dependency graph for Moriarty, or an accepted proof architecture.

proposals.title: One invoice partial, with payment and duties separated
bookReference: B08-EXACT-MANUSCRIPT-SECTIONS.json: The Seven Layers at a Glance, lines 272-298
B08-EXACT-MANUSCRIPT-SECTIONS.json: The Proof Core: Layers 4, 5, and 6, lines 2340-2353
proposals.sourceSupport: invoice-fixtures.json specifies opening duties of 100 CASH invoice and 10 CASH reserve, default partial 35, fee 2, and source-versus-proposed funding. scenarios.json specifies 110−35−2=73 against 65+10=75, versus proposed 112−35−2=75. V2-COPY says the fee discharges no debt and a remaining duty is financial progress, not a missing proof.
proposals.websiteMapping: Connect Layer 2's financial rule and Layer 4's arithmetic to Layer 7's transaction consumer. Present Layer 5 and Layer 6 as the proof and cryptographic questions whose exact adopted wording remains a security review matter.
proposals.readerCopy: The seller receives 35 CASH. The fee recipient receives 2 CASH, making the escrow debit 37 CASH. The fee repays nothing: invoice duty falls from 100 to 65 CASH, reserve duty stays at 10 CASH, and total duties are 75 CASH. With 110 CASH funded, 73 remains, 2 short of those duties. With a proposed 112 CASH funding mode, 75 remains against 75 of duties for this one partial. The 112 mode is a proposed funding policy, not an S12 action. The remaining invoice duty is debt still owed, not a missing proof.
proposals.interaction: Use payment 35 as the initial worksheet value. Keep 110 and 112 funding modes visibly distinct. Show seller receipt, fee receipt, gross debit, closing cash, invoice duty, reserve duty, total duties, and backing gap as separate values. Add an explanation that each further partial costs another 2 CASH and that full payment uses finish().
proposals.diagram: Two parallel funds-flow rows: 35 CASH to seller and 2 CASH to fee recipient, both leaving escrow as a 37 CASH gross debit. A separate duties panel moves invoice 100→65 and leaves reserve at 10; compare remaining cash 73 or proposed 75 with total duty 75.
questions: Should the page label the 112 mode 'proposed extra fee budget' consistently with the source fixture?
Confirm final wording around backing policy and the source's non-negative-custody rule with the financial/security owners.
proposals.limits: Local arithmetic from supplied fixtures only. It does not run Moriarty, create or verify a proof, settle a transaction, or establish ledger state. S12 has no 112-funding action or reserve-duty-return action; each later partial needs another fee allowance. Network fees, collateral, proof-claim min-ADA, and the V2 thread reserve are separate.

proposals.title: Use the same layer questions across five cases
bookReference: B08-EXACT-MANUSCRIPT-SECTIONS.json: The Seven Layers at a Glance, lines 272-298
B08-EXACT-MANUSCRIPT-SECTIONS.json: The Proof Core: Why Layers 4, 5, and 6 Are Inseparable, lines 2831-2848
proposals.sourceSupport: scenarios.json provides the illustrative invoice, DEX, issuance, loan, and treasury values, financial effects, and dependencies. It explicitly says these are future proof roles rather than separate existing proof producers; DEX, issuance, and loan have no supplied source program.
proposals.websiteMapping: A five-card selector reuses the same educational layer questions while changing the financial story: fee and residual duty for invoice; per-order limits, pool rounding, and allocation for DEX; supply, distribution, and separate duties for issuance; accrual, repayment, and fee for loan; quotient, transfers, and reserve duties for treasury.
proposals.readerCopy: Follow the amounts that define each transition: two DEX owners offer 100 A each and require at least 90 B net; an issuance example creates 300 units under a cap of 1,000 and distributes 180 plus 120; a loan example moves from 100 debt to 105 after accrual, then to 70 after a 35 repayment; a treasury example checks 23 = 3×7 + 2 and shows the resulting transfers and duties. Unissued capacity is not debt, and a fee is not repayment.
proposals.interaction: For each case, expose four tabs or highlights: authorized inputs, arithmetic/constraints, proof question, and consumer/financial effects. Keep the exact-case values visible and mark values requiring a source or external observation as unavailable until supplied.
proposals.diagram: Five case cards feed into one reusable seven-question map; each card has a short funds-and-duties strip. Do not draw one producer icon per named Strand role.
questions: Which exact amount examples are retained after financial and security review?
What exact asset identities and allocation rules would a DEX example need before it can be more than illustrative?
What signed policy and actual mint-policy behavior would an issuance example need?
proposals.limits: Worked examples only. No live price, source program for DEX/issuance/loan, independent proof producer, application mint policy, or ACTUS conformance is established.

proposals.title: Show inputs, private witness, and authenticated premises
bookReference: B08-EXACT-MANUSCRIPT-SECTIONS.json: The Seven Layers at a Glance, lines 272-298
B08-EXACT-MANUSCRIPT-SECTIONS.json: Trust Decomposition: Seven Weaker Assumptions, lines 4502-4527
proposals.sourceSupport: The manuscript treats witness handling as Layer 3. V2-COPY distinguishes computation over supplied values from authenticated ledger facts and outside observations, and records privacy and implementation limitations as technical matters.
proposals.websiteMapping: Pair Layer 3 with Layer 7 for all five cases: identify the values a calculation consumes, the private data intended to stay private, the state that must be tied to a transaction, and any external fact that needs an issuer, authentication path, or freshness rule. Example: loan accrual needs a period/rate and any variable-rate provenance; DEX pool arithmetic needs pool state and exact rounding; invoice payment uses predecessor duties and actual outputs.
proposals.readerCopy: A proof checks a calculation over the values it receives. The application still needs to show where those values came from. The transaction supplies ledger facts; an outside price, delivery record, or other observation needs a named source and a rule for when it is current.
proposals.interaction: Open an input drawer with columns 'calculation input', 'where it comes from', and 'who or what must authenticate it'. Let each case expose its own unknowns without implying a value is known or current.
proposals.diagram: Inputs flow into a witness-and-constraint panel; a separate transaction and source panel feeds the consumer's binding checks. Never portray the proof alone as authenticating a price, delivery, signer, or ledger state.
questions: What exact user-facing distinction between private witness, public statement, transaction fact, and external observation is approved?
Which witness side-channel wording is accurate for this project's implemented prover path?
proposals.limits: This is conceptual education, not a privacy guarantee, side-channel assessment, source authentication, or evidence that an external observation exists.

proposals.title: Connect encoding, proof system, cryptography, and setup
bookReference: B08-EXACT-MANUSCRIPT-SECTIONS.json: Universal versus Circuit-Specific Setups, lines 609-621
B08-EXACT-MANUSCRIPT-SECTIONS.json: The Proof Core: Layers 4, 5, and 6, lines 2340-2353
proposals.sourceSupport: The manuscript explains coupling across arithmetic representation, proof-system design, and cryptographic primitives. V2-COPY reports a forgeable single-party current test setup, unknown total setup count, no production ceremony in supplied records, local invoice proof evidence, and open source-to-circuit/VK correspondence.
proposals.websiteMapping: Link Layers 1 and 4–6 to each financial example's relation, but keep claims about Groth16, ceremony structure, concrete setup count, cryptographic guarantees, and measured costs in a technical status section pending the assigned security review.
proposals.readerCopy: The financial rule, the way it is encoded, the proof system, and the cryptographic building blocks shape one another. The seven labels help explain those concerns; in an implemented system, several choices are closely coupled.
proposals.interaction: Show a compact 'design and evidence' panel with distinct statuses for source-level description, local proof evidence, design proposal, and open technical questions. Link this panel to each case without adding a live cost or setup estimator.
proposals.diagram: Layers 4–6 appear as a connected design group, with links to setup (Layer 1) and consumer verification (Layer 7). A separate evidence panel states current status and unknowns.
questions: Which security claims from the manuscript survive Opus 5.5 review for this product and implementation?
What precise wording should describe the class-0 forgeable test setup, unknown circuit/setup count, and open T3 correspondence?
Should the main page name Groth16, or reserve it for the technical section with its exact limitations?
proposals.limits: No production setup, circuit inventory, setup count, proving/verification cost, cryptographic audit, or independent source-to-circuit proof is established by this educational mapping.
